7. Statistical Analysis
7.1 Analysis Population
All subjects are to be randomized in a 1:1 fashion to either clopidogrel monotherapy or aspirin
monotherapy groups. All primary and secondary endpoints will be analyzed both on an
intention-to-treat basis (all subjects analyzed as part of their assigned treatment group). For
intention-to-treat analysis, all subjects who signed the written informed consent form and are
randomized in the study will be included in the analysis sample, regardless of whether the
correct treatment was administered, or whether crossover occurred.
Per-protocol population will be defined as population who did not violate the study protocol.
The definition of protocol violation is as follows.
1 Interruption of allocated antiplatelet agent within the study periods
2 Administration of DAPT (aspirin plus clopidogrel) in both arms without any clinical events
3 No anti-platelet agent is used within the study periods (except participants who newly
needed anticoagulation therapy due to atrial fibrillation or others)
4 Administration of aspirin in the clopidogrel group within the study periods
5 Administration of clopidogrel in the aspirin group within the study periods
6 Use of antiplatelet agent in different dose other than specified in study protocol
7 DES was not used in the index procedure

Analysis with per-protocol population will be performed as exploratory and sensitivity analysis
for that of intention-to-treat population.

7.2. Primary Endpoint Analysis
Primary endpoints (the rates of MACCE) will be analyzed on an intention-to-treat basis, and
then, per-protocol basis. All analyses will be performed 1 year after the last patient enrollment.

precision. P-values will be reported only for the primary analysis, and effect estimates will be
the focus of the interpretation. Kaplan-Meier survival curves will illustrate time-to-event data,

The secondary endpoints will be analyzed on an intention-to-treat basis and per-protocol basis
at 1 year after the last patient enrollment. Secondary endpoints including all-cause and cardiac
death, MI, definite/probable stent thrombosis, TLR, TVR, any revascularization, CVA, BARC

Sample Size Calculation
Power calculations are based on a superiority comparison for the primary endpoint of major
adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) in the clopidogrel monotherapy group
than in the aspirin monotherapy group. We expected that the rate of the MACCE would be 4.0%
in the aspirin monotherapy group and 3.0% in the clopidogrel group based on the previous
trials that evaluated the rates of adverse events in patients who completed the standard duration
of DAPT and who were at high risk for recurrent ischemic events after PCI with current-
generation DES.4-6 With this assumption, we calculated that a total of 5000 patients (2500 per
each group) would be needed for the trial to have 82% power to detect a relative risk reduction
by 25% in the primary endpoint in the clopidogrel group compared with the aspirin group at a
two-sided alpha level of 0.05 (calculated using R, gsDesign package). Even if the number of
enrolled patients exceed 5000, we will continuously enroll in subjects until the end of the
enrollment period (accrual time: 3 years) to ensure the power of the study.
<Summary>
1) Primary endpoint: Time to occurrence of MACCE
2) Expected annual rate of MACCE:
3) Clopidogrel (3.0%) vs. Aspirin group (4.0%)
→ 25% relative risk reduction
4) Total study time: 4 years
5) Accrual time: 3 years
6) Follow-up will be done till 1 year after the last patient enrollment.
7) Alpha = 0.05 (2-sided), β = 18%, Power (1- β) = 82%
8) 1:1 Randomization
9) Assumed drop-out rates: Total 2.5%

Treatment of Missing Values

Primary endpoint (the rates of MACCE) will be analyzed on an intention-to-treat basis, and
then, per-protocol basis. All analyses will be performed 1 year after the last patient enrollment.
The primary hypothesis test was performed by means of a stratified Cox proportional-hazards
model. The confirmatory two-sided significance level was set at 5%. Results will be presented
as hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) to quantify the effect size and its
precision. P-values will be reported only for the primary analysis, and effect estimates will be
the focus of the interpretation. Kaplan-Meier survival curves will illustrate time-to-event data,
with complementary effect estimates provided. The cumulative incidence of the primary
endpoint was computed according to the complement of the Kaplan-Meier estimates of event-
free survival with log rank test. All primary and secondary endpoints will be analyzed on a per-
patient basis.
The secondary endpoints will be analyzed on an intention-to-treat basis and per-protocol basis
at 1 year after the last patient enrollment. Secondary endpoints will be analyzed using Kaplan-
Meier survival with log rank tests. While no formal adjustment for multiple comparisons will
be applied, the results for secondary endpoints will be interpreted as exploratory. Effect
estimates (HRs and 95% CIs) will be emphasized, and P-values will not be presented. Total
medical cost will be analyzed using an independent t-test. A pre-specified subgroup analysis
will be performed according to pre-specified 11 variables (clinical presentation, age, sex, body
mass index, diabetes mellitus, renal dysfunction, left ventricular systolic function, bleeding risk,
complex coronary lesions, duration of DAPT maintenance before randomisation, and use of
proton pump inhibitor). As requested during the revision process, two extra subgroup analyses
(post hoc) were added (duration of DAPT before randomisation >18 months vs. ≤18 months;
and type of P2Y12 inhibitor before randomisation).

Per-protocol population will be defined as population who did not violate the study protocol.
The definition of protocol violation is as follows.

a) Interruption of allocated antiplatelet agent within the study periods
b) Administration of DAPT (aspirin plus clopidogrel) in both arms without any clinical
events
c) No anti-platelet agent is used within the study periods (except participants who newly
needed anticoagulation therapy due to atrial fibrillation or others)

9.3 Patient Discontinuation (Withdrawal Criteria)
Once enrolled, each patient should remain in the study until the required follow-up period is
complete. However, all patients have the right to withdraw at any point during the study without
penalty or loss of benefit. The investigator may discontinue any patient at any time if medically
necessary. Data obtained to the last follow-up will be used for the analysis. It will be
documented whether each patient completed the clinical study. If the study treatment(s) or
observations are discontinued in any patient, the reason will be recorded, and the data
coordinating center must be notified promptly.
The following events will result in the termination of the patient's follow-up:
• Patient voluntary withdrawal
• Patient withdrawn by investigator as clinically indicated.

It is imperative to obtain complete follow-up data for all patients, whether they receive their
assigned treatment. Every attempt should be made to collect follow-up information, except for
those patients who specifically withdraw consent for the release of such information. All
procedures and laboratory specimens or tests requested for evaluation after enrollment in the
study should be carried out, when possible, whether a patient continues to receive treatment
according to the protocol. Patients will not be replaced in this trial.

9.4 Lost to Follow-up
Patients that do not complete the scheduled follow-up visits and have not officially withdrawn
from the study are considered lost to follow-up; this term does not apply to missed visits. Site
personnel should make considerable effort to locate and communicate with the patient using
all available methods (ex, telephone, emails, and postcards). The following contact procedure

If the patient misses 2 consecutive scheduled contact time points and the above-mentioned
attempts at communicating with the patient are unsuccessful, the patient will be considered
lost to follow-up.

10. Study Protocols
After the patient has been enrolled in the present study, patients assigned to the clopidogrel
group will receive clopidogrel 75 mg once daily and those who assigned to the aspirin group
will receive aspirin 100 mg once daily. The detailed schedule of measurements for this trial is
located in section 11. It is recommended that each enrolling investigator review the most
recently updated IFU and assess the contraindications, warnings, and precaution sections for
treating potential patients. Regardless of the allocated arms, the best available medical
treatment will be performed according to the current guidelines. Any adjunctive pharmacologic
treatment will be left to the operator's discretion.

It is intended that all statistical analyses specified in this protocol will be performed. However,
it is conceivable that due to the study observations, some scheduled analyses may not be
performed. In addition, study observations or analysis results may suggest the need for
additional statistical analyses of the collected study data. In either case, deviations
(subtractions or additions) from the planned statistical analysis will be fully described in the
final clinical study report. Furthermore, any additional analyses performed beyond those
specified in this protocol will be descriptive in nature and will not include hypothesis testing for
the purposes of inferential conclusions.

20.2 Protocol Amendments
In case any revisions to the protocol are required, protocol amendments will be provided to
investigators by the steering committee prior to implementation. The Primary investigator(s)
will be responsible for notifying the IRB of the protocol amendment with administrative
changes or obtaining IRB approval of the protocol amendment with changes in patient care
or safety. Institutional Review Board acknowledgements/approvals must be documented in
writing prior to implementing protocol amendments.

5.2. Study Timetable
The assumed trial enrollment period is approximately 3 years. Follow-up will be performed till
1-year after the last patient enrollment.

5.3. Randomization
Patients will be screened for eligibility, and, if qualified, written informed consent will be
obtained from all patients. If patients agree to participate in the study, 1:1 randomization
between clopidogrel and aspirin stratified by participating center and presentation at the index
procedure (MI vs. non-MI) will be performed via Web-based randomization program (Apache
2, PHP 5.3, and MySOL5; S-Soft) in permuted blocks, with block sizes of four.

6. Sample Size Calculation
Power calculations are based on a superiority comparison for the primary endpoint of MACCE
in the clopidogrel monotherapy group than in the aspirin monotherapy group. We expected
that the rate of the MACCE would be 4.0% in the aspirin monotherapy group and 3.0% in the
clopidogrel group based on the previous trials that evaluated the rates of adverse events in
patients who completed the standard duration of DAPT and who were at high risk for recurrent
ischemic events after PCI with current-generation DES.16,17,24 With this assumption, we
calculated that a total of 5000 patients (2500 per each group) would be needed for the trial to
have 82% power to detect a relative risk reduction by 25% in the primary endpoint in the
clopidogrel group compared with the aspirin group at a two-sided alpha level of 0.05
(Calculated using R, gsDesign package → figure below). Even if the number of enrolled
patients exceed 5000, we will continuously enroll in subjects until the end of the enrollment
period (accrual time: 3 years) to ensure the power of the study.

7.3. Secondary Endpoint Analysis
The secondary endpoints will be analyzed on an intention-to-treat basis and per-protocol basis
at 1 year after the last patient enrollment. Secondary endpoints including all-cause and cardiac
death, MI, definite/probable stent thrombosis, TLR, TVR, any revascularization, CVA, BARC

7.4. Censoring
Patients not experiencing a primary endpoint event during this time interval will be censored
at the time of death, last contact date (for subjects withdrawing consent of lost to follow-up),
whichever comes first.

7.5. Treatment of Missing Values
The primary analysis of the study endpoints will be used as a Cox proportional hazards model
adjusting for stratification factors. No imputation methods will be used to infer missing values
of baseline variables. For the study endpoints, patients lost to follow-up and subsequently lost
to assessment of study endpoints will be considered to be censored in the estimation of
Kaplan-Meier event rates.
